title: Prefetch Manifest and Lean SDK Handshake — PRD sketch
body:
Purpose

Sketch PRD proposing a compact, explicit "prefetch manifest" and a minimal SDK-server "lean handshake" to enable predictable, low-latency streaming + tool-calling for constrained clients (mobile, edge, embedded). Goal: reduce tail latency and token cost for common call patterns while preserving graceful degradation and developer ergonomics.

Background & problem
- Many clients request multi-step tool-heavy workflows (e.g., fetch metadata -> call external tool -> synthesize) and suffer repeated cold-start work: model rewarm, KV cache miss, tool init.
- Current hosted streaming surface sends tokens progressively but lacks a small, typed negotiation channel to express which resources to prefetch and which fidelity is acceptable.
- SDKs try ad-hoc prewarming; inconsistent behavior across languages, wasteful bandwidth, and poor observability.

Goals (built-in success metrics)
- Latency: 25–40% reduction in 95th percentile end-to-end latency for targeted tool flows in pilot apps.
- Cost: 10–20% token cost reduction via prefix caching and selective model variant prefetch.
- Ergonomics: single small SDK surface (<= 3 methods) that developers can opt into without major app changes.
- Safety/compatibility: false-positive prefetching should be limited and revert gracefully.

Key idea: Prefetch Manifest
- A compact declarative manifest (JSONL-friendly) that lists intended calls and resource hints: model_variant, expected_prefixes (sha256 short), tool_ids, expected_seq_len, priority, privacy_tier.
- Manifest is sent at session start or can be appended mid-session. Example (sketch):

{"manifest_version":"1","entries":[{"id":"search-step","tool":"web_search_v2","want_model":"gpt-8-lite","prefix_hash":"3f5a...","priority":10}],"ttl":60}

- Server uses manifest to: prewarm KV cache, route to capacity pools (dedicated vs hosted), warm tool connectors, and attach prefetch.score telemetry to subsequent responses.

Lean SDK Handshake (surface)
- Minimal calls: PrefetchManifest.upload(manifest), Handshake.status(session_token) and Cancel(prefetch_id). Rationale: small surface to maintain language SDK simplicity and reduce integration cost.
- SDKs expose local cache hooks: onManifestAccepted(metadata), onPrefetchProgress(percent), onFallback(reason).

Streaming interplay and structured output
- Manifest-driven prefetch allows server to start incremental partial outputs earlier (e.g., emit an initial structured header saying which tools are ready and which are degraded).
- Structured tool-calling frames include an optional prefetch.confirmation block that client SDK can use to render optimistic UI.

Telemetry and signals
- New metrics: prefetch.accept_rate, prefetch_hit_rate (per manifest entry), prefetch_latency_ms, prefetch_waste_tokens.
- Instrumentation: add prefetch.* tags to tracing spans and integrate with Console dashboards and Optimize recommendations.

Security and privacy
- Manifests may include private resource hints. Treat manifests as user data subject to retention/policy. Provide per-manifest privacy_tier: public|sensitive|restricted. Use KMS tagging for restricted prefetch jobs.

SDK ergonomics notes
- Lightweight: keep binary size small for mobile by providing manifest helpers as optional module.
- Backward compatible: manifest calls are optional; server falls back to default routing when absent.
- Offline-first: SDK should cache last manifest and attempt opportunistic prefetch when device is charging/wi-fi. Provide TTLs to prevent stale prefetches.

Operational concerns and rollout
- Canary feature flags per-customer to gate prefetch routing and billing. Initial limited rollout to 5 pilot customers.
- Billing: optional discounted prefetch token bucket (customer-paid) vs on-demand prefetch paid from normal usage. Need billing experiment.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How to best express unknown/conditional flows (e.g., tool called only if search yield > 0)? Consider boolean predicates vs lightweight branching hints.
- Should prefetch be charged immediately or only when consumed? Need finance input (JIRA:PRIC-432).
- Tool init cost vs model warm: prioritize warm path ordering—policy decision.

Next steps / action items (owner: Maya Patel)
- Align with Serving Runtime: define prefetch job API and capacity tagging (eng-serving-runtime) — owner: Liam. (Due 2026-01-15)
- Prototype SDK surface in JS and Kotlin, include onManifestAccepted hooks (devexp) — owner: Jia. (Due 2026-02-01)
- Run 3 small pilot flows with SolutionsEng to measure p95 improvements (customer-success) — owner: Priya. (Due 2026-03-01)

Appendix: short integration example (JS pseudocode)
const manifest = {version:1, entries:[{id:'meta', tool:'kb_search', want_model:'gpt-8-lite', priority:8}]};
await RedwoodSDK.PrefetchManifest.upload(manifest);
// SDK emits onManifestAccepted -> UI shows "warming…"
// Later streaming responses include {prefetch_confirmation:{id:'meta', status:'ready'}} blocks

This doc is a sketch; goal is to capture concrete engineering workstreams, minimal SDK needs, and an ops-safe rollout plan. Feedback requested on manifest shape, billing model, and predicate language for conditional prefetch.
